newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slip, hurt by weaker dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares slip, hurt by weaker dollar.

text.p: German shares sank to small losses in early dealings on Monday, unsettled by the dollar's sharp decline in Asian dealings and waiting for Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony this week.
The 30-share DAX index was down 1.85 points at 3,182.24 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 20.85 points at 3,182.94 points.
Despite the initial losses, some traders said they did not expect the drop to worsen dramatically over the day.

Dealers also noted turnover was very limited, making it hard to label the price move the start of a correction. March DAX futures, which move in line with the cash market, were firmly supported at 3,180 points.
Traders generally expected the market to remain stable ahead of Greenspan's testimony to the U.S. Congress on Wednesday and Thursday.
Attention will be fixed on what Greenspan has to say about U.S. stock market market activity, especially since previous comments about the market briefly interrupted the advance.
A lack of fresh corporate news was also expected to keep the market in a sideways trend.
Dollar-sensitive chemical and engineering companies were under the most pressure. The biggest decliner was chemicals group Hoechst AG, which fell 1.70 marks to 70.15 marks.

Volkswagen AG, Europe's largest carmaker, was up eight marks at 808 marks. The carmaker said at the weekend it would make an announcement on Wednesday about how it would deal with allegations of corruption in its purchasing department.
